items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Willard Alexander booked my group, basically.

ctx.x: In 1950 you joined the Basie band and he had recently disbanded his big band…
Yeah, that’s when… Murphy:…in favor of small groups.
Right, that was Willard Alexander’s idea because big bands were starting to fold one after another with the advent of Rock and Roll.

items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: Willard Alexander came to me and said, 'I’m putting together a small group for Count Basie... So he put me with the Basie Band in 1950'

ctx.x: There wasn’t that much room but if you were at the top of your game, then maybe you could get enough chances to play.

Yeah. And even when things were really fading here for bebop so to speak, or modern jazz, we could go to Europe, and we’re always recognized in Europe. Seventy percent of my income was in Europe for many years. 1950 around that area is when I decided I wanted a big band, but Willard Alexander came to me and said, “I’m putting together a small group for Count Basie because big bands are kind of folding.” Which I didn’t want to believe. I wanted my big band because I idolized Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw. But he…
